As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Chelsea gift the ball away inside their own half and Leao drives forward. The Portuguese forward moves into the Chelsea penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is blocked.

A big, big chance for Chelsea to take the lead. A long ball is played forward in behind the AC Milan defence and Pedro gets the better of De Winter inside the Milan penalty area. It is then a one-on-one chance with Torriani but Pedro hits it straight at the Milan goalkeeper. Torriani should have come to claim that long ball and then Pedro should probably have buried that opportunity.

Chelsea win their third corner of the game as Palmer’s cross from the right takes a couple of deflections off AC Milan defender. Captain Caicedo has trotted over to take it out on the left. He sends it into a good area but a foul on the AC Milan keeper Torriani is given against Pedro.

Neto clips a free-kick into the AC Milan penalty area, which is chested down by Pedro. The Brazilian holds the ball up well inside the box before winning a corner. Chelsea play it short and Palmer crosses to the back post, where Palestra wins Chelsea another corner, this time out on the left.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

Palestra, who has joined Chelsea this summer from Atalanta, is proving his versatility today; he has mostly operated for Chelsea at right-back so far this pre-season but he is starting at left-back in this game.

Camarda is played in behind the Chelsea defence and tries to get the better of Fofana inside the Chelsea penalty area but the ball just runs out of play across the byline before Camarda can square the ball.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1858. Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

By RIATH AL-SAMARRAI, CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:30 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:22 EST, 7 November 2026

Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break.

There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation.

But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch.

If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot.

In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke.

The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise.

Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull

The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced

For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6)

Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly

Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6)

Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz

For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition.

Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack.

It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull.

Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting.

Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend.

It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them.

Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious.

Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz

Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London

Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City.

Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors.

'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta.

'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that.

'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.'

Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy.

The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor.

Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position.

On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty.

'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it.

'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.'

The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick.

A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right?

Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective.

None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak.

Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour.

By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening.

First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner.

Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

#1857. Rio Ngumoha interview: Liverpool youngster on Chelsea exit, Max Dowman and how Lamine Yamal changed the game

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Rio Ngumoha wears a cheeky smile as he sits in his England puffer jacket at Hotspur Way and discusses his upbringing, his hopes and dreams, and the lasting legacy of a fellow teenager.

Ngumoha, 18, is just a year younger than the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal and argues: “What he is doing [has] changed football for young players.

“Seeing what he can do so young inspires me and all the other young players in how we can just play freely. The way he plays, it’s like it’s his pitch. It’s a good challenge.”

He has been rewarded for fine form at Liverpool with another England call-up this month, and the absence of Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke gives Ngumoha a good chance of earning plenty of game time on the right wing against Croatia and Yamal’s Spain.

Tuchel has a glint in his eye whenever he speaks about Ngumoha and from the sidelines when the teen is readying himself to come on, you can tell they share a bond.

“He knows I’m quite talented, which is good,” he says. “Every time I come on he lets me be expressive, be free. I have the belief from him.”

Playing under Tuchel for England and Andoni Iraola for Liverpool are “similar” but their “language is a bit different”, he says, explaining that at England “it is a lot more structured, because you know the manager doesn't have enough time to get his ideas across — so that's why we have a lot more meetings, which is understandable.

“It was definitely difficult at the start when he [Iraola] came in [at Liverpool], but we had to adapt quickly.”

Ngumoha says he has played “a couple of times” against English football’s other talked-about wonderkid, Arsenal’s Max Dowman, but believes he has “played more with him than against him. Max is a top, top, top talent, a top player, and he'll definitely go on to reach many heights. We text each other if [one of us] scores.”

Describing his own playing style as “fearless” is not brash but simply the truth of the matter, and it is this confidence in his ability to go past players that led Tuchel to bring him along for the summer’s pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, handing him his debut, before a call-up for the last international break and another this month.

It was in Florida that he struck up a friendship with Fulham’s Josh King, the pair of them reunited with England this month.

#1856. Nicolo Tresoldi: Italy call-up “a possibility” as Roberto Mancini issues update amid Germany competition

By Oliver Thomas | 09 Nov 2026 16:38

Italy head coach Roberto Mancini has provided a fresh update on the national team’s hopes of persuading Nicolo Tresoldi to represent the Azzurri over Germany.

The 22-year-old Club Brugge star was born in Cagliari to an Italian father and Argentine mother of Italian descent before he moved to Germany at the age of 13 for his mother's work.

Tresoldi joined Hannover 96 at youth level before spending three years in the senior team between 2022 and 2025, making 80 first-team appearances.

The striker has since elevated his game to new heights in Belgium with Club Brugge, while he has represented Germany at Under-19 and Under-21 level, scoring 19 goals 35 appearances across all tournaments.

Tresoldi’s standout performances have sparked a dual international tug-of-war between Italy and Germany, and he is still undecided on his long-term allegiance.

However, Mancini is optimistic that Italy can secure Tresoldi’s services following a conversation he and Claudio Ranieri - the technical director of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) - had with the in-demand striker.

Speaking at a press conference on Monday ahead of Italy resuming their UEFA Nations League campaign this week, Mancini told reporters: “I have spoken to [Tresoldi], as has Ranieri. He needs to feel that he wants to play for Italy.

“Given that he was born in Italy and his father played for Italy [and won the European Under-21 Championship], I think there could be a possibility.

“Ultimately, it is the player who has to make the decision. He knows that we believe he could be important for us.”

Tresoldi has once again been called up to Germany’s Under-21 squad for the November international break ahead of friendly matches against Belgium and Croatia.

The next international break is scheduled for the end of March 2027, giving Tresoldi plenty of time to mull over whether he wished to represent Italy or Germany - now managed by Jurgen Klopp - at senior level.

Both Italy and Germany are understandably keen to win the race for Tresoldi, who has established himself as one of the most prolific strikers in Europe over the last 12 months or so.

Last season, Tresoldi inspired Club Brugge to their 20th Belgian Pro League title after scoring 13 goals in 30 matches to win the division’s Golden Boot award.

He has since carried his prolific form in the new campaign, netting 14 goals in 17 appearances across all competitions, including eight strikes in 11 league games.

Tresoldi is currently the joint second-top scorer in the Champions League with five goals in just four matches, including a memorable hat-trick in a thrilling 4-3 away victory over Inter Milan last month.

Known for his elite penalty-box movement and high-intensity pressing, Tresoldi is understood to have caught the attention of some of Europe’s biggest clubs, including Premier League champions Arsenal.

Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur have also been credited with an interest in Tresoldi, who is valued at €35m (£29.2m) by transfermarkt and is under contract at Club Brugge until June 2029.

There was a long review by the referee Michael Oliver, who was sent to the pitchside monitor to consult with the video assistant referees at Stockley Park.

#1854. Amorim opts against press conference ahead of Genoa vs. Milan – the reason

There will be no pre-game press conference with Ruben Amorim today, as confirmed by Milan’s press office yesterday.

It was hard to miss Amorim’s disappointment and anger after Milan’s defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday evening, being very honest in his interview after the game. While he took on some of the blame, he criticised the players for not having the right attitude and mentality.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s something that has been echoed by others, including the Milan legend Billy Costacurta, who criticised the entire squad for not doing the red and black shirt justice. In any case, the Rossoneri need to get back on the horse on Sunday, taking on Genoa away from home.

As confirmed by Milan’s press office last night, in a message sent directly to us and other news outlets, there won’t be any press conference with Amorim today. It’s something he usually hosts on the eve of each game, but there is a reasonable explanation for the cancellation.

Generally speaking, we are not huge fans of Amorim opting to cancel the press conference, but it comes down to the congested schedule. He spoke to the media before and after the Ferencvaros game, so he didn’t feel like a press conference less than 48 hours later would give much.

It’s not the first time a press conference has been cancelled this season due to that very reason, and it’s something we have seen with other managers at Milan too. In other words, it was kind of expected even if, without a doubt, the journalists would have had questions for Amorim.

#1853. Virgil van Dijk issues transfer latest as Liverpool contract expiry looms

Virgil van Dijk maintains that he is relaxed about his Liverpool contract situation.

The Dutchman’s deal at Anfield expires at the end of the current campaign, and there have been no indications so far that he will sign an extension.

The central defender has been one of the Reds’ first-choice players ever since he arrived at Anfield back in 2018, joining from Southampton for £75million.

The No4 has taken on the captain’s armband on Merseyside following Jordan Henderson’s departure, with the 35-year-old racking up 282 appearances for the club since his move.

Now, he has issued an update on his contract status, insisting that he is not panicking over his future.

"I feel good, but it’s not about me at the moment," the centre-back said. "Let’s see. I’m not in any panic whatsoever. I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing.

"Let’s see what the season brings. I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case.

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment, but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything."

Van Dijk withdrew from the Netherlands’ Nations League camp with an injury - Liverpool confirmed on Monday - and manager Andoni Iraola will be hoping that the issue is minor, meaning that his skipper is able to face Manchester United on November 22.

"Physically I’ve been struggling with a little niggle the last couple of weeks but I do everything in my power to be out there," Van Dijk added.

#1852. Man Utd news: Red Devils 'plot ambitious move' to appoint new No.2 for Michael Carrick

By Carter White | 09 Nov 2026 16:54

Manchester United are reportedly interested in hiring Bayern Munich assistant Aaron Danks to help under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick.

The 20-time English champions are sitting in 18th position in the Premier League standings following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at the Theatre of Dreams on Sunday afternoon, when the hosts completed another Old Trafford comeback.

Patrick Dorgu's last-minute equaliser was celebrated with considerable vigour, however, Man Utd remain in a worrying situation near the foot of the table, winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight contests.

It appears that the Red Devils have a real fight on their hands to retain their Premier League status, with United legend Roy Keane criticising head coach Carrick following the eight-goal thriller against Villa.

With the Premier League now taking a two-week break for international action, Man Utd have some time to recovery and prepare for a crunch clash with arch rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester United's hierarchy are set for 'high-level discussions' during the international break, analysing the start to the season and laying out a plan for the months ahead.

The future of head coach Carrick will be a major talking point for sporting director Jason Wilcox and head of recruitment Christopher Vivell, who have been sounding out potential replacements recently.

Former Newcastle United and Bournemouth boss Eddie Howe is supposedly of interest to Wilcox, whilst ex-Germany and Bayern Munich coach Julian Nagelsmann is said to have caught the eye of recruiter Vivell.

However, there is a reality in which Man Utd choose to stick with current leader Carrick, who has stated that he expects to take charge of the squad past the international break, despite an awful start to 2026-27.

It is understood that the club's boardroom are eyeing up a swoop for Bayern assistant Danks, who would arrive at the Theatre of Dreams to provide support for Carrick in his time of desperate need.

Working together at Championship outfit Middlesbrough in the past, Carrick and Danks possess a good footballing relationship, with the Bayern Munich man having plenty to offer the wounded English giants.

That being said, the direction of Red Devils travel is unlikely to change too much without significant change - whether that be to the playing staff or the people pulling the strings in the boardroom.

There is no doubt that the majority of United supporters would prefer a clean break from Carrick's faltering plans, instead of an attempt to strengthen the 45-year-old's backroom ranks.

#1851. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

📃 Le onze de départ pour cette rencontre de préparation face à Manchester United. #PSGMUN pic.twitter.com/LodcDM1Yrm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

#1850. Arsenal star reveals how Mikel Arteta is 'different to any other manager'

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Christos Tzolis has revealed how Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is different to any other manager he has played under.

The Greek joined the Gunners last summer in a £34million move from Club Brugge, that saw the winger return to England after a spell at Norwich City.

The forward had an underwhelming period at Carrow Road before moving to Belgium, where he lifted the Pro League title last season, which helped propel him to the Emirates Stadium.

He has just returned from a hamstring injury on international duty that kept him out for a month, but he made a return to action in the 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis has spoken of his admiration for Arteta being a big part of why he wanted to move to north London, and he explained to Novasports how the Spaniard differed from any head coach he had had previously.

"He does a lot of things before the matches, some alert games, in the locker room to see the players' readiness,” he said.

“He always has different ideas before each game and approaches it differently.

"I mean, I haven't seen that with any other coach. In the first talk we had in the summer, he asked me about my life, about my life outside of the game as well, about football of course.

“And I spoke for 45 minutes, for sure, and 10-15 minutes as coach, so he was very open to hearing what I had to say."

#1849. Official: Pavlovic will miss Milan’s game against Genoa due to injury

Strahinja Pavlovic’s absence for tomorrow’s game between AC Milan and Genoa has now been confirmed, with the shoulder injury still bothering him.

After playing through the pain in Milan’s 3-1 win against Inter, Pavlovic was left out of Milan’s squad for the mid-week clash against Ferencvaros. The goal was immediately clear: to recover in time for Sunday’s game against Genoa at the Marassi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While Milan were hoping to see positive results in training today, it has instead been confirmed by the club that the Serbian won’t be called up by Ruben Amorim due to severe stomach pain. He has been called up by Serbia for the upcoming break, but it remains to be seen if he will travel.

As it has now been confirmed that Pavlovic will miss out, Sankhoun Diawara can prepare knowing that he will definitely start tomorrow. The same goes for Pervis Estupinan, who will take the Frenchman’s role in the left-back position, at least according to Gazzetta dello Sport.

Davide Bartesaghi is an option too but he didn’t have the best of games against Ferencvaros on Thursday, and there might be some tiredness there. In any case, it’s a shame not to have Pavlovic available for what is clearly a very important game for the Rossoneri.

Not to mention that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori are already on the sidelines, leaving Milan with few options at the back.

#1848. Man United transfer news: Red Devils could move for "quick" and "powerful" Premier League centre-back next summer

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 17:59, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 18:03

Manchester United are reportedly huge admirers of Nottingham Forest's Murillo and could make a move for the centre-back during next summer's transfer window.

Murillo, 24, has provided one assist in 11 appearances for Forest this season, while he has represented the Reds on 125 occasions since arriving from Corinthians in the summer of 2023.

According to Man United's former chief scout Mick Brown, Man United have been keen on the Brazilian "for quite a long time now", and a "huge offer" could potentially be forthcoming at the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

"Murillo is somebody Man United have liked for quite a long time now," Brown told Football Insider. "Obviously they're not the only ones, because at his best he is a top class player, and he would certainly be an improvement on the players they've got at the moment.

"He's quick, powerful, aggressive, excellent on the ball, can pass, isn't afraid to get stuck in, it's pretty much everything you want from a centre-back. At his best, when you compare him to Lisandro Martinez who plays in the same position, there's such a big difference in quality.

"So for Man United, he is somebody they're going to be very keen on and I have a feeling that if they came in with a huge offer, it would give Forest something to consider.

"They're a good side, Forest, but they're down the wrong end of the table and if that continues then their best players might be tempted away.

"If there are any suggestions that Murillo could be allowed to move, then Man United should be all over it, because he would be such a big improvement for them."

Murillo has made 103 Premier League appearances for Forest, scoring three goals and registering three assists in the process.

Man United are set to overhaul their defence at the end of the season, and it is not impossible to imagine three new centre-backs arriving at the club.

Both Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire are out of contract next summer and could leave on free transfers, while a decision needs to be made on Matthijs de Ligt, who has recently returned to action after almost a year on the sidelines through injury.

Man United are also set to bring in a new left-back and right-back next summer as part of a major revamp, with Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot both potentially moving on.

#1846. Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 12:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:24 EST, 7 November 2026

Just when Newcastle looked set for victory after Jacob Murphy had borrowed Amar Dedic's bow to arrow them into a late lead, they turned the weapon on themselves.

After a week in which Dedic, Bosnia's answer to Robin Hood, had made headlines when pursued by police for wandering around the Northumberland countryside with his hunting gear, the Geordies were ready to rob the good folk of west London after Murphy found the target ten minutes from time.

Less than three minutes later and they were picking the arrow from their own foot. William Osula failed to protect possession and allowed Fulham to enter the penalty area. Then, with the ball bouncing around the goalmouth, it was home substitute Rodrigo Muniz who pounced to punish Newcastle's scruffy defending.

'Slapstick', visiting boss Matthias Jaissle later called it.

The German also said that his team deserved to win but you got the impression he was relieved to emerge without defeat, especially as the performance was improved on the back of a run of four losses in five.

Newcastle's second-half spirit also showed a response to a week of noise centred on dressing-room unrest, not to mention Dedic's police drama.

Jacob Murphy thought he had won it for Newcastle after scoring late on at Craven Cottage

Rodrigo Muniz netted moments later after sloppy defending from Newcastle, earning a 1-1 draw

Matthias Jaissle's side were much improved but must cut out the errors to win matches

And Jaissle was right in that his team could have left with three points had master archer Harvey Barnes not missed a hat-trick of chances.

Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno 7; Castagne 6 (Tete 77, 5), Affengruber 6, Bassey 6, Robinson 5; Berge 6, Charles 6; Bobb 6 (Sessegnon 78, 6), King 7 (Palacios 72, 5), Iwobi 6; Garcia 4 (Muniz 65, 8)

Subs not used: Lecomte, Andersen, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, Kevin

Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 7; Dedic 6, Thiaw 7 (Schar 85, 6), Burn 7, Hall 6; Nico Gonzalez 5 (Miley 61, 6), Steur 7 (Fernandez-Pardo 74, 5); Murphy 8, Wissa 6 (Willock 61, 5), Barnes 6; Osula 5 (Elanga 85)

Subs not used: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Bazoumana Toure

The winger is the player to whom they'd want those opportunities to fall, too. But twice before half-time, when denied by Bernd Leno from close range, and then again when lashing wide after the break, he failed to give his side the advantage.

Murphy corrected his team-mate's finishing when capitalising on a loose pass from Cesar Palacios and slamming into the bottom corner from 25 yards, but that joy was short-lived.

In truth, there hadn't been much joy to behold all afternoon. The draw keeps both sides in the bottom half of the table, and that is where they will likely stay.

The first half, in particular, had very strong last-on-Match-of-the-Day vibes.

Newcastle thought they had a 33rd-minute lead when Dan Burn stole in at the near post to flick home from Murphy's low cross.

What the officials had spotted at the far post was linebacker Yoane Wissa pinning defender Timothy Castagne, and so playing Burn onside. It was the right call, even if Jaissle disagreed

'I learned that word here, a 'soft' decision. In my eyes, it was not right,' he said. 'But I was pleased with our complete commitment and togetherness.

'We grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on. We showed the fundamentals.'

Dedic twice came close to creating goals with teasing crosses from the right, and you wondered if he would have mimicked Barnes' trademark archer celebration had they been converted.

He was kept away from the media post-match, but Jaissle did say: 'He played well, right? It (the bow & arrow incident) didn't affect him. He was not aware of the rules. We don't need to make a big deal out of it.'

Fulham's Josh King was included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday, the club's first Three Lions call-up in eight years. He, however, now needs a scan on a tight groin before learning if he's fit enough to feature.

Did the 19-year-old play like a would-be England international? He was his side's best player in the first half, even if that was a low bar to hurdle. One volley would have raised the roof had it gone in, so sweet was the connection from 20 yards. Lukas Hornicek needed every inch of his 6ft 6in frame to dive and save. And that, too, was a recurring theme, Newcastle's reliance on the big Czech to bail them out when giving up chances.

Like Newcastle, however, Fulham simply weren't good enough to take them.

#1845. 'Many were skeptical': Dejan Kulusevski reveals Tottenham staff doubts in shock injury admission

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Dejan Kulusevski has revealed that some Tottenham staff doubted that he would be able to recover from the knee injury that kept him out for 18 months.

The Swede made his long-anticipated comeback to action in Spurs’ 1-0 win over Coventry last month after a lengthy lay-off that had him wondering whether he would ever be able to kick a ball professionally again.

The time on the sidelines forced the forward to go as far as telling his mother that he thought his career was over at the mere age of 26.

And as Kulusevski began losing faith in his recovery process, he has now revealed that some in north London felt the same way.

“There were many who didn’t believe it, many were skeptical. Even at the club,” he told Fotbollskanalen.

“I’ve been disappointed in people during this period, but at the same time I have to forgive everything.

“Sometimes you wish you’d received more help and so on. But at the same time, I understand we’re all part of a business.

“I’ve moved on and I love being at the club. I received a really good welcome when I came back.”

Kulusevski has returned to international duty this week after missing the World Cup last summer.

He has confirmed that while he is able to complete a full 90 minutes in both Nations League games against Bosnia and Herzegovina and Poland, that will not be the case when he runs out for Graham Potter’s side.

“I’ll get to play some minutes in both games,” he continued.

“Around 30 minutes in each. That’s what’s been said. It’s better than zero, so I’m happy.”

“I actually can play 90 minutes in both matches. But that’s what I can do. I’m not the one who decides.”

#1844. Michael Carrick future: Review 'ongoing' at Man United - what will be the outcome?

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 18:29

Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox is reportedly leading the review into Michael Carrick's future at Old Trafford.

A disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, with the team winning just one of their first 10 league games of the season.

Man United did manage to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League last week, though, before twice coming from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday, and the season has now been interrupted by an international break.

There is huge uncertainty when it comes to Carrick's future, with the sporting department at Old Trafford now reviewing the head coach's position.

According to The Guardian, Wilcox is leading the review, with chief executive Omar Berrada also being consulted, before a recommendation is made to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Carrick was expected to be sacked by Man United off the back of the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25, but he was allegedly given three games to save his job - the trip to Chelsea in the Premier League, followed by the games against Roma and Villa.

It is understood that Eddie Howe is Wilcox's number one choice to replace Carrick, should a change be made, but that is not thought to be a view universally shared by the decision-makers.

Man United are next in action at Anfield on November 22, facing Liverpool in the Premier League, before tackling Sporting Lisbon away from home in the Champions League.

November will then conclude with a home league game against Brentford.

"We’re in November. I don’t like the situation we’re in or the results we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it. We haven’t won enough games but I expect to move forward," Carrick told Sky Sports News after the draw with Villa.

"We’ll keep working on the things we’ve been working on, and tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."

The positions of both Wilcox and Berrada have also been called into question due to Man United's ongoing struggles, and the pair are facing uncertain futures.

There remain calls from the club's supporters for the Glazer family to sell their share of the 20-time English champions, but there are no indications at this stage that will occur.

As it stands, Carrick is likely to remain in charge of Man United for the Liverpool game, with the Englishman still being backed despite the team's struggles this season.

#1843. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

#1842. Photo: Leak suggests Puma will go for bold design with Milan’s 2027-28 third kit

The design of AC Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season has been leaked, according to a report, featuring a black base and yellow details.

The 2027-28 season will be the last with Puma as Milan’s kit partner, as an agreement worth €50m per year has been reached with Adidas from 2028-29 onwards. It’s a switch that many fans have longed for, but right now, the focus is on whether Puma will end their tenure at the top or not.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The reality is that a lot of the Puma kits, especially the ones in recent years, have been praised by the Milan fans for their design. There’s certainly no bad blood between the parties and as such, Puma is working very hard to deliver a strong output for the last season.

This morning, an image of what is believed to be Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season surfaced, courtesy of the usually credible Footy Headlines. The base is black with grey paint splatter effects, while the details are yellow/neon-yellow.

It doesn’t really remind us of any previous kits that Milan have worn, especially since it’s a rather bold design (but it’s a third kit, after all). Compared to the current third kit, for example, the 2026-27 edition is much more muted and clean, whereas this is very lively.

Only the chest image has been leaked so far, so we will have to wait a little longer to see the full shirt. Let’s also remember that this is an early leak and that the final design will likely differ a little. Usually, the final version tends to look better.

#1840. Mauricio Pochettino 'agrees to be new Manchester United manager' after overnight talks

Manchester United are reportedly finalising an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has been identified as the club’s first-choice candidate to replace Michael Carrick, who is set to be sacked.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have flown out to meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco, where he resides and company INEOS have offices in the principality.

Carrick is expected to again take charge of a depleted first-team training session at Carrington today, while work is concluding on hiring his replacement.

According to The Athletic, United spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Pochettino’s representatives, with no major obstacles expected and a final agreement expected.

The Guardian reported on Tuesday evening that Pochettino was keen to become the next Man Utd manager.

However, the club have yet to approach US Soccer, who would be entitled to around $10m (£7.4m) in compensation through an exit clause in the Argentine’s contract.

Pochettino, currently in charge of the United States national team, is contracted until 2030 but is reportedly keen to take the Old Trafford job. His coaching staff would also require compensation if he leaves.

According to iNews, Pochettino was heavily backed by the Glazer family to replace Carrick in the Man Utd dugout.

The Glazers had stepped back from direct involvement in footballing decisions since selling shares to Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS investment, but it appears the family are set for a more active role after further regression on the pitch.

The former Southampton, Chelsea, and Tottenham boss has previously spoken about his desire to return to the Premier League and previous Manchester United interest in his services.

It could be a case of third time lucky for Pochettino, who missed out on the Man Utd job in 2018 and 2022 to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag, respectively.

Compensation would also need to be worked out for his coaching staff, who are expected to cross the pond with Pochettino to take up the role.

#1839. Arsenal star addresses January exit rumours as Mikel Arteta talks confirmed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Martin Zubimendi has dismissed speculation that he is close to leaving Arsenal.

The midfielder has not started a Premier League game for the Gunners this season, having fallen behind Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly in the pecking order.

With minutes hard to come by, there have been suggestions that Zubimendi was unhappy and looking for a way out of Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid are among the clubs understood to be monitoring his situation and some reports in Spain have claimed that Zubimendi was nearing a return to his homeland.

However, speaking to Marca while on international duty, the 27-year-old revealed that is “not at all” true.

“To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press,” Zubimendi said.

“I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

“Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

“Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.”

Asked if he will remain at the club until at least the summer, Zubimendi added: “Yes, I hope so. I’m happy there.”

Zubimendi started 33 of Arsenal’s first 34 league matches last season, making a big impact in his first season in England.

However, he dropped out of the side in the final weeks of the campaign as Myles Lewis-Skelly earned Mikel Arteta’s trust in midfield.

Zubimendi’s task has been made tougher this season by the £75million arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, but the Spaniard has not been surprised by his lack of opportunities in the opening months of the campaign.

Arsenal star reveals how Arteta is 'different to any other manager'

England legend demands 'lifetime ban' for Arsenal star after squad snub

When Arsenal youngsters will play for England after double selection boost

“I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season,” Arteta said.

“As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me. He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side

“I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

“I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.”

As well as not starting in the Premier League, Zubimendi has only made two appearances in Europe. One of those was an eight-minute cameo against Napoli.

However, he insisted: “I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

“Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

“I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

“I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.”
