#1807. Barnsley vs Oldham Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 10 Nov 2026 02:26

In the final round of fixtures in the EFL Trophy group stage, Oldham Athletic will head to Oakwell to take on Barnsley.

The visitors are on the back of an FA Cup victory over Sheffield Wednesday at the weekend and are already qualified for the knockout rounds, while their hosts are unable to progress.

Barnsley return to action at Oakwell on Wednesday aiming to build on a much-needed cup victory at the weekend, albeit while being unable to progress in the EFL Trophy in their final group outing.

After the return of promotion-winning manager Daniel Stendel over the summer, the South Yorkshire outfit have endured a poor start to their League One campaign, currently sitting 23rd having earned just nine points from their first 12 outings and only won two of those alongside seven defeats.

Those wins came consecutively with the most recent being the beginning of September, before the Reds went on an 11-game winless run in all competitions including nine losses, culminating in four straight league defeats and a draw against Oxford United.

Non-league Aldershot then visited Oakwell in the FA Cup first round at the weekend, and Stendel's side finally ended their rut in comfortable fashion, progressing with a 7-2 victory as Cameron McGeehan netted a hat-trick alongside Vimal Yoganathan's brace and goals from Reyes Cleary and Rylan Brownlie.

Now unable to progress in the EFL Trophy, having lost their first two games to Leeds United Under-21s and Fleetwood Town in the midst of their rut, but needing to rebuild confidence before their return to league action in a bid to escape the drop zone, Barnsley will hope to make it back-to-back home cup wins on Wednesday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, arrive in South Yorkshire in search of another cup win over third-tier opposition having already booked their place in the knockout stage of the EFL Trophy.

In their second season back in the EFL, after a 10th-placed League Two finish last time around and an EFL Trophy group-stage exit, Oldham Athletic currently sit 18th in England's fourth tier having won four and lost seven of their first 14 outings.

That is alongside a perfect start to the new EFL Trophy campaign, as they guaranteed a top-two group finish with a 1-0 home win over Fleetwood Town and a 4-2 triumph over Leeds United Under-21s.

Micky Mellon's side are now on the back of consecutive victories too, firstly returning to winning ways in the league last week by beating Northampton Town away from home, before hosting third-tier Sheffield Wednesday in the FA Cup at the weekend and winning 2-1 after extra time with Callum Kavanagh putting them ahead in normal time and Will Sutton scoring the decisive goal in the 110th minute.

Oldham Athletic now head into a second straight cup game in search of another victory to finish the group stage with a perfect record before turning their focus back to climbing up the League Two table.

Desperate for consecutive wins, Stendel will field a similar starting XI from the weekend's cup win, with Ben Hamed Toure and Fabio Jalo still out.

Brownlie may come in from the start after his goal off the bench, while McGeehan and Yoganathan will support a lone striker again after scoring three and two goals respectively at the weekend.

They should again join danger man Reyes Cleary, while Daniel Johnson joined Luca Connell in midfield on Saturday while Patrick Kelly was rested from the start.

Oldham may also be unchanged from their FA Cup victory with Ryan Delaney and Keenan Appiah-Forson still among those sidelined.

Kavanagh will continue to lead the line after his opener against Sheffield Wednesday with Mike Fondop regularly joining him up top.

Injuries and suspensions left the Latics unable to complete their bench on Saturday, meaning the likes of Oliver Norburn and Tom Pett may not be afforded rests.

Slicker; Okedina, Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Connell, Kelly; Yoganathan, McGeehan, Cleary; Adeyemo

Oldham Athletic possible starting lineup:

Hudson; Sutton, Daniels, Monthe; Scott-Morriss, Pett, Norburn, Robson; Chilvers; Fondop, Kavanagh

Barnsley's comfortable victory over Aldershot was a great first step in their bid to reverse their fortunes, and likely to continue with a full-strength XI in search of another win, we back them to get over the line in a tough game on Wednesday.

#1806. Arsenal transfer news: PSG close door on Gunners target Ibrahim Maza

By Axel Clody | 10 Nov 2026 06:47

Paris Saint-Germain have decided to close the door on Ibrahim Maza, because Luis Campos did not at all like an approach from the camp of the Algeria international and Bayer Leverkusen.

Luis Campos has decided to shut down the file after Maza’s father and Bayer Leverkusen wished to go through the Stellar agency to check PSG’s interest. PSG also claim never to have been the ones to initiate a concrete approach for the player.

After Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s injury, PSG interest in Maza was reported. Sky Sport Germany even revealed that the French capital club had made contact with the Algerian’s entourage. The two-time European champions were following the situation of the Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder closely and even considered a move as early as the January transfer window.

The path to the 20-year-old gem therefore appeared very serious. However, the file is reportedly no longer really live. According to information from Sacha Tavolieri, an episode behind the scenes has completely cooled the French side.

‘Ibrahim Maza’s father and Bayer Leverkusen wished to bypass the initial framework of discussions by getting back in touch with Paris, via the Stellar agency, in order to “check” the French club’s interest’ - the Belgian journalist revealed. It was an approach that Campos did not appreciate at all.

The Paris sporting adviser has reportedly decided to end the exchanges because this way of working does not match how PSG want to handle their business. The Portuguese has sent a clear message to Leverkusen and the camp of the Algeria international, the Maza file is now closed.

‘PSG would never have initiated a concrete approach to sign the player’ - the French club have even reportedly insisted, according to Tavolieri. Maza’s big dream of joining PSG will therefore not come true in the January window and could even be forgotten for a while after this episode.

Arsenal have also been linked with Maza. In late September, TEAMtalk reported that the Gunners were prepared to accelerate a bid for the 20-year-old, with Tottenham also monitoring the situation.

Leverkusen are determined to keep their midfielder and would reportedly only discuss a sale for around £60m. PSG’s exit would remove one potential rival, but the price tag remains a significant hurdle for any suitor.

#1805. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

Double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

Blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

The first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

We are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

Possession: Wolves 52%-48% BlackburnShots: 10-4Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 9-7

An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

Both teams scored when the other seemed on top slightly.

Wolves have probably shaded it with those efforts from Lopez and Mane which went narrowly over.

Plenty to think about for the two managers.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the new Championship season.

"They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt

Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

Wolves: Bentley; Trippier, Mosquera, T.Gomes; R.Gomes, André, Munetsi, Möller Wolfe; Lopez, Mané; Armstrong.Substitutes: Sá, Bueno, Jiménez, Lima, Doyle, Chirewa, Djiga, Tchatchoua, Edozie.

Blackburn: Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Forshaw, Montgomery; Afolayan, Cantwell, Morishita; Gudjohnsen.Substitutes: Pears, Ribeiro, Tavares, Morsy, Fevrier, Carter, Henriksson, Ohashi, Garrett.

These do not look good if you are a Blackburn fan; these are their attacking statistics and rankings in the Championship last season:

Goals: 42, 23rdxG performance: -13.9, 24thShots on target: 146, 23rdShot conversion: 7.9%, 22ndChances created: 368, 21st

Near the bottom of the league in every single one of those pretty much.

A debut for our brand new away kit 🤩#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Qxyvw1jAgi

Former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes has died aged 79 in the last week and the club he played 382 times for is paying tribute to him tonight:

Paying tribute to a Wolves legend on tonight's matchday programme 🧡 pic.twitter.com/VEHciTuOZq

"We know what we are doing" 🤝Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is confident in his side ahead of his the first Championship game of the season 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/2m12gsJ2y8

"We're ready for a strong performance" 💪Wolves defender Kieran Trippier and Blackburn's Sam Morsy preview their opening game of the season clash 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/I5t1J9Gapp

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ

Saturday:Bolton vs PrestonBristol City vs MillwallCharlton vs DerbyMiddlesbrough vs LincolnNorwich vs West BromPortsmouth vs QPRStoke vs SwanseaSheffield United vs Birmingham

Sunday:Watford vs SouthamptonBurnley vs West Ham

🔢 Team news...2⃣ changes✅ Kristi Montgomery & Andri Gudjohnsen come in🆕 Sam Morsy on the bench🤕 Augustus Kargbo, Dion De Neve, Scott Wharton, Moussa Baradji, Mathias Jorgensen & Lewis Miller on the injured list#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/esyE5Fibqc

☝️ One change from Port Vale🇳🇴 Wolfe in at LB🇪🇸 Hugo misses out with minor groin issueOur line-up for tonight's @EFL Championship opener 📋 pic.twitter.com/oRpIymUw1k

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#1804. Opposition insight for Genoa-Milan: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

Genoa are the next opponents for AC Milan and given the Rossoblu’s recent form, they certainly could have faced them at a better time.

Ruben Amorim and his men really need to pick themselves up with a win tomorrow afternoon, which would at least allow them to build on the derby win in the league. In the Europa League, however, that chance is already gone as they lost to Ferencvaros.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, getting the three points might not be the easiest task as Genoa have been in red-hot form lately, and will certainly use all of the support from their fans at the Marassi tomorrow.

➤ Manager: Daniele De Rossi ➤ Form (all comps): W-L-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Osmajic – 4 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Colombo and El Shaarawy – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: None.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was bought permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but did make sure to express his respect for the Rossoneri.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

#1803. Prediction: Norway vs Wales

In what is a must-win Nations League showdown for both camps on Saturday evening, Norway will welcome Wales to Oslo.

With a stacked schedule from across the continent this weekend, there are plenty of attractive Nations League betting promotions available.

Ahead of Saturday’s League A showdown from Oslo, you can find all of the key Norway vs Wales H2H stats here.

Verdict: Martin Odegaard over 0.5 shots on target

Starting with the hosts, punching a World Cup quarter-final ticket over in North America during the summer, Norway rightfully received plenty of plaudits from across the globe. However, despite opening their Nations League adventure with an action-packed 3-2 victory at home against historic rivals Denmark on September 24th, Stale Solbakken’s men have come crashing back down to earth in a concerning fashion. Last seen signing off September’s extended international break with a 2-1 loss at the hands of European giants Portugal, Norway have now lost each of their previous three consecutive League A showdowns and they suddenly have a real battle in the race to keep hold of their top-flight status. Opening October with a 2-1 defeat against Wales, Saturday’s hosts have have plenty of pressure on their shoulders when they return to Oslo this weekend.

Getting back to his best with reigning Premier League champions Arsenal this season, skipper Martin Odegaard will lead Norway out in Oslo and earn a 78th international cap on Saturday evening. Notching nine top-flight strikes for Manchester City since opening up the 2026/27 campaign, striking superstar Erling Haaland will spearhead Solbakken’s charge in the final third.

Already registering 11 direct Bundesliga goal contributions for RB Leipzig (four goals, seven assists), the red-hot Antonio Nusa will join Haaland in attack. Completing a season-long loan switch to French outfit Brest, Egil Selvik should keep his spot between the sticks.

As for the visitors, while Wales might have claimed that stellar 2-1 victory at home against Norway last month, it appears that was just a minor boost for Craig Bellamy’s squad. Immediately crashing back down to earth as they signed off September’s extended international break with a toothless 1-0 defeat against Denmark, the former Burnley coach has seen his squad lose three of their four Nations League appearances and they find just their goal difference ahead of Saturday’s opponents. Suffering World Cup qualifying heartbreak back in March, Wales are also searching for an essential clinical edge in the final third. Getting their Nations League charge underway with another 1-0 loss against Portugal on September 24th, Bellamy’s men have recorded more than a single strike in just one of their previous eight matchups across all competitions.

In what is a real blow for Wales, Wrexham striker Kieffer Moore has been forced to withdraw from Bellamy’s squad due to injury. However, the Dragons have welcomed back the Leeds United duo of Joe Rodon and Daniel James this month.

Picking up a costly Nations League booking against Portugal last month, Swansea City defender Benjamin Cabango will miss out through suspension. Despite still waiting to open his Premier League account after completing a big-money summer switch to Everton, Brennan Johnson could play a leading role in the final third.

While Wales might have clinched a shock 2-1 win when they welcomed Norway to Cardiff for their reverse Nations League showdown last month, the Dragons travel to Oslo on Saturday evening pencilled in as a landslide underdog. Two camps who are facing a real battle in the race to keep hold of their League A status, we look set for what is a must-win battle this weekend. With Norway remarkably losing all of their previous three consecutive Nations League showdowns, Saturday’s hosts will be calling on their all-star attack to spearhead their charge on home soil.

Verdict: Martin Odegaard over 0.5 shots on target

#1802. How Mauricio Pochettino really feels about Man Utd job revealed after Michael Carrick sack update

By Lewis Blain | 10 Nov 2026 07:05

Mauricio Pochettino could emerge as a leading contender to become Manchester United's next manager if Michael Carrick is dismissed.

The former Tottenham Hotspur boss is currently in charge of the United States Mens National Team (USMNT), but reports suggest he would be 'interested' in returning to the Premier League.

With Red Devils chiefs expected to make a decision on Carrick's future during the international break, Pochettino's stance could become increasingly significant.

According to talkSPORT, Pochettino would be keen on taking charge at Old Trafford should United decide to part ways with Carrick.

The Argentine signed a contract extension to remain with the USMNT until the next World Cup in 2030, but his name is expected to feature prominently in the club's search for a replacement.

The Athletic's David Ornstein has also revealed that United expect a managerial change before their next fixture against Liverpool, and that work is already underway on potential replacements.

Pochettino, 54, is among the candidates expected to be considered, alongside former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann.

United have yet to officially confirm a decision on Carrick, but his position has become increasingly difficult to defend after a disappointing start to the campaign.

The Red Devils are 18th in the Premier League with only eight points from ten matches, having won just once in the competition this season.

Although Carrick rescued a point against Aston Villa with a dramatic 4-4 draw at the weekend, United's hierarchy are expected to hold further discussions before deciding whether to make a change ahead of the trip to Anfield.

Pochettino would represent a considerable upgrade on Carrick in terms of managerial experience, having previously worked at Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

He is arguably a more attractive appointment than Howe, too, given his experience of competing at the highest level and his familiarity with the demands of managing a major Premier League club.

However, whoever replaces Carrick will inherit largely the same problems.

United's squad remains unbalanced, with significant holes to fill and inconsistency across several positions, including left-back, out wide and up front. A change in the dugout might provide an immediate lift, but it will not suddenly resolve those obvious weaknesses.

Pochettino could offer a clearer tactical identity and greater experience, but he would need time, and more importantly, substantial investment to turn United into genuine challengers again.

Ultimately, appointing a proven manager is an important first step, but the club's recruitment and long-term planning must improve if another managerial change is to deliver lasting success.

#1801. Premier League star's career criminal brother beats Home Office bid to deport him to Africa - as he awaits trial for kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery

Published: 03:45 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 8 November 2026

The street criminal brother of a Premier League star has beaten a Home Office attempt to deport him to Africa - by citing his own human rights.

The gang member and aspiring rapper, now in his twenties, was the subject of a concerted four year attempt by the government to send him to his family's country of origin in West Africa because of his shocking criminal record.

The young man, who has never held down a job, is currently in prison for dangerous driving and carrying a knife - while awaiting yet another court case accused of kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery.

During his teens he had played academy football for several Premier League teams but while his brother went on to make it and is now a multi-millionaire, the man instead got sucked into street crime.

And he has been involved in so much anti-social and criminal behaviour since then that he has even incurred a number of gunshot wounds.

But the wannabe rapper has managed to win a long-running deportation bid by the Home Office to kick him out of Britain as an undesirable - arguing that this wouldn't be fair as all his significant ties are here.

A Premier League footballer - who cannot be named for legal reasons - has seen his career criminal brother living in Britian beat a Home Office attempt to deport him back to West Africa

The Home Office first targeted him for deportation in 2022 after he was sentenced to 20 months in jail having been caught with a sword in his waistband, which in turn meant had breached an existing order about his criminal behaviour.

They lost that attempt to get him out of Britain but appealed - and have now lost that appeal too.

The gang member is 'healthy and capable' according to a judge but has never worked - in stark contrast to his hugely successful brother, a full international footballer who has made countless top flight appearances.

A court heard the foreign national has a 'sustained history of criminal offending involving repeated breaches of Criminal Behaviour Orders, possession of offensive weapons, breaches of licence conditions, recalls to custody, and recent charges. He has a history of offending with knives since the age of 17'.

Totaling his various jail terms together he has spent three of the last eight years prison.

But despite his ongoing recurrent criminality, the Home Office has failed in its latest attempt to deport him after a judge ruled he is 'socially and culturally integrated' into the UK and a return to his home country would leave him 'very much an outsider'.

The immigration tribunal decided he would face 'very significant obstacles to integration' in his home country and prevented the government from deporting him by ruling it would breach his human rights.

That decision came despite it emerging that he has an uncle in the country and grew up with a familiarity of the country, including its culture and food, while his mother maintains links to the country and visited as recently as 2024.

But the judge said the 'significance of these ties should not be exaggerated' because he has never been there.

They said his social and cultural identity 'has been almost entirely formed in the UK and by British culture' - even though he was born overseas and his family come from West Africa. The Home Office is appealing the decision and so the brother could still face deporation.

The knife criminal first arrived in the UK in 2006 after being born in another country where he doesn't have nationality.

He is in a relationship with a British woman with whom he shares a baby.

Their child was born in February but the rapper has only met them twice because he remains incarcerated.

There is no evidence that having a partner or child has reformed his criminal ways, a court heard.

The Home Office argued he is a healthy young adult capable of work who has a familiarity with the culture of his home country and has family ties in the country who could provide guidance and support.

But the judge concluded it would breach his human rights because he has never lived or visited and would be an outsider if returned.

#1800. Man United: Neville laments ‘rinse and repeat’ cycle at Old Trafford

By Axel Clody | 10 Nov 2026 07:07

Gary Neville has once again directed criticism at the leadership of Manchester United. For the club idol, the instability that has surrounded the club in recent years will not be resolved simply by another change of manager.

Speaking to NBC, the pundit said the owners do not know how to handle the situation of Michael Carrick and pointed to failings in different areas of the football structure.

The sporting situation helps explain the discontent. United arrive at the international break in the relegation zone of the Premier League, with only one win in the competition. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, in which Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time, avoided a defeat but was not enough to ease the pressure on the club.

The situation contrasts with six months earlier, when Carrick took charge on an interim basis and guided the team to third place. The drop in performance has revived doubts about his future, but Neville believes the discussion about the manager distracts from deeper problems.

In Neville’s assessment, Manchester United are repeating a cycle of hope and frustration.

The arrival of a new manager usually generates optimism in the first few months, but the results and the internal problems come back. For that reason, the former full-back believes that a possible exit for Carrick would not, by itself, resolve the crisis.

‘When the new manager comes in, everybody’s happy for a couple of months and then all of a sudden, six months later, it happens again’ - he said. The pundit recalled that the club has been through eight managers in 12 years and questioned the insistence on treating a change in the dugout as the solution.

Neville did not necessarily argue for Carrick to stay. His point was precisely to highlight the lack of clarity about the way forward, regardless of the decision on the current manager.

‘Michael could leave, Michael might stay, we don’t know, the ownership don’t have a clue what to do’ - he said. The list of figures who have passed through the club since the departure of Sir Alex Ferguson helps illustrate the scale of the instability.

‘It’s rinse and repeat. Ruben Amorim, Erik ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Michael Carrick’s in the job now, Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, Ralf Rangnick.'

'Some of them are world-class managers who have had success, there are a lot of promising young managers there, ex-players who know the club as well. None of it has worked because if you recruit badly, if you’ve got a poor performance department, poor recruitment department, you’ve not got leadership that is strong right through the spine of the football club, you will fail.’

The former captain also stressed that the lack of results cannot be explained simply by the quality of the managers appointed. In his view, some of the names who have passed through Old Trafford had a history of winning trophies and experience at the highest level, but did not find a structure capable of supporting a sporting project.

The discontent with the running of the club also appeared in the stands at Old Trafford. During the draw with Aston Villa, supporters displayed banners aimed at the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with a clear message: ‘We do not want a new stadium, we want new owners’.

The protests reflect a demand that goes beyond results on the pitch. The Glazer family remain the majority owners of Manchester United, while Ratcliffe and INEOS took control of football operations after acquiring a minority stake in the club. The leadership structure also includes names such as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Neville also cited the need for alignment between the different levels of the institution. In his view, it is not enough to hire a big-name manager or bet on young players with potential if the decisions taken by the board do not follow a common direction.

‘Every organisation in the world will fail if you’ve not got an aligned leadership from top to bottom, your board and your ownership right the way through to the person who is stood on the pitch’ - Neville concluded.

The criticism puts the spotlight back on a question that has followed Manchester United since the end of the Ferguson era: the difficulty of turning one-off changes into a consistent sporting project.

While the club tries to find an answer to the situation of Carrick, Neville’s assessment is that the debate about the manager cannot replace a wider discussion about who makes the decisions and how football is run at Old Trafford.

#1797. Chelsea: Fantasy Premier League sparks internal row over Joao Pedro injury

By Axel Clody | 10 Nov 2026 07:15

Joao Pedro has been missed by Xabi Alonso. Out of action since mid-October because of an injury, the Brazilian striker has become indirectly involved in a curious episode involving Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

According to the BBC, Chelsea had to send an email to their employees warning them about the possible consequences of using inside information to pick FPL line-ups, which can reveal which players are unavailable or close to returning, as happened with Joao Pedro on 24 October.

Before the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham at Stamford Bridge in the eighth round of the league, the number nine became a surprise absentee because of a muscle problem in his thigh that was only revealed hours later. The problem is that several Fantasy Premier League content creators had already pointed out Joao Pedro’s absence because of the make-up of the line-ups of Chelsea members.

Influencers said they had seen evidence that Morgan Rogers and other names at the club had removed the Brazilian from their FPL squads, although Chelsea had released no official information about the striker’s injury before kick-off against Tottenham.

Asked at a press conference, the Spanish manager said he was unaware of the situation because he is not interested in fantasy teams. ‘I am not into the fantasy team thing, so I didn’t know that’ - Alonso told BBC Sport.

This is not the first time Chelsea have suffered from leaked information.

During the Liam Rosenior era between January and April, line-ups were leaked before the two games against Paris Saint-Germain on 11 and 17 March, in the last 16 of the Champions League, when Chelsea lost 8-2 on aggregate.

It later emerged that Marc Cucurella’s barber had revealed on social media that Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer would be absent for the match against Brighton, who won 3-0 at the American Express Stadium in the 34th round of the 2025-26 Premier League, on 21 April.

He found out the information in a conversation with his client, who now plays for Real Madrid.

Regarding Fantasy Premier League, Chelsea consider the case involving the number nine to be isolated and do not expect it to lead to restrictions.

The club’s directors believe the episode can be avoided in future through greater awareness among players and Chelsea staff, in order to prevent new line-up leaks.

In FPL, people earn points based on the real performances of players in the competition. Each user receives £100m in the game to build a squad of 15 players (11 starters and four substitutes), and every goal, assist and clean sheet earns points. Users also have to choose a captain each round, whose score is doubled.

It is estimated that more than 11 million people play Fantasy Premier League, which has become a darling of the football ecosystem. Despite strict rules that prohibit betting, the competition offers no specific guidance to clubs on how those involved should behave around the game, nor on whether they should take part individually. Each club handles the matter on its own.

Crystal Palace are continuing to explore their managerial options following the uncertainty surrounding Pierre Sage's position at Selhurst Park.

Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have reportedly emerged as two additional candidates being considered by the Eagles.

Askou, who only took charge of Toulouse in the summer, could represent another relatively inexperienced appointment in the Premier League.

According to Sky Sports, Palace have added Askou and Werner to their shortlist, alongside favourite Thomas Frank, as they consider potential replacements for the under-fire Sage.

Werner was most recently in charge of RB Leipzig before being dismissed in June 2026, while Askou joined Toulouse from Motherwell during the summer.

His previous managerial experience includes spells at Vendsyssel, Torshavn, Horsens and Goteborg, alongside assistant coaching roles at Slavia Prague and Copenhagen.

#1795. Serie A preview: Genoa vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

A tough away trip awaits AC Milan on Sunday afternoon, hoping to restore some order against an in-form Genoa side.

What many hoped would be a positive week quickly turned into a negative one, as Milan failed to build on the derby win against Ferencvaros. In other words, they need to respond with a strong performance against Genoa, which is easier said than done.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim didn’t have a press conference earlier today due to the tight schedule, so there are no new takeaways from him. Judging from the post-match interviews on Thursday, however, he’s expecting a lot more from his players at the Marassi.

Game date: Sunday, November 8 Kick-off time: 15:00 (CET) Venue: Stadio Luigi Ferraris Referee: Davide Massa (VAR: Camplone)

It’s been said for quite a few games now, but Amorim certainly isn’t being helped by the injury situation. In total, seven players will be on the sidelines for the game tomorrow, including key players like Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic and Alexis Saelemaekers.

Milan were hoping to recover the Serbian for this one, but severe stomach pain is keeping him on the sidelines after missing the Ferencvaros game too. Considering that Matteo Gabbia and Fikayo Tomori were already on the injury list, it’s certainly not ideal.

Mike Maignan will be back between the sticks, at least, after serving a suspension in the Europa League. He will have a defence of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan ahead of him, with the left flank being the main worry there.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will be demoted to the bench as Luka Modric will be back from start, partnering with Yunus Musah in a tandem. Adrien Rabiot, meanwhile, is expected to have a slightly more advanced role.

Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic will be the danger men on the attacking flanks, looking to replicate their success against Inter in the derby. The same cannot be said for Goncalo Ramos, who instead needs to get going with his goalscoring after bagging just two league goals so far.

In terms of firepower on the bench, Amorim could turn to Davide Bartesaghi, the aforementioned Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse. Francesco Camarda will also be there, of course, but whether he can be categorised as an impact player is a different question.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Modric; Moreira, Rabiot, Pulisic; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Torriani, Bouyer, F. Terracciano, Vladimirov, Bartesaghi, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Chukwueze, Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Pavlovic, Saelemaekers, Terracciano, Tomori.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

Nevertheless, the poor star has been cancelled out and it’s possible that De Rossoneri just needed some time, especially after losing key players like Jeff Ekhator (to Juventus) and Brooke Norton-Vuffy (to Hull City). The Serie A veteran Ruslan Malinovskyi also waved goodbye as his contract expired.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was signed permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but he did make it clear that Genoa cannot get too cocky.

Genoa (3-5-2): Bijlow; Marcandalli, Ostigard, Vasquez; Ellertsson, Baldanzi, Frendrup, Traore, El Shaarawy; Colombo, Osmajic.

Predicted bench: Stolz, Sommariva, Messias, Otoa, Sabelli, Puczka, Amorim, Meichtry, Mitaj, Vitinha, Sow, Drameh, Ehizibue, Wiafe, Venturino, Havel.

This will be the 157th encounter between the two sides, with Milan looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind at 37 wins. 48 games have ended all square, which is a tally that has increased lately.

In the last five games, there have been three draws (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1), but the good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games. The five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Rossoblu since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. They both left the club on loan this summer, so they won’t be of any help tomorrow.

In the game before that, Rafael Leao (another player who’s no longer in the team) rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa; only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

Starting with Milan, and at the back, I think we should keep an extra eye on Diawara. He did well in the derby but after switching to centre-back for the Ferencvaros game, his display just wasn’t good enough. He will have the same position tomorrow and we need to see an improvement.

Further up the pitch, Moreira showed in the derby that he can be just the X-factor that Milan need, and this game should be an even better one for him (at least on paper). The cameo against Ferencvaros was positive despite the result, so hopefully he can build on the last week.

As for the home side, I’m curious to see Traore in action again. He definitely had some very good games for Sassuolo against the Rossoneri and with more consistent playing time at Genoa, he could rediscover that spark which made him so special.

Finally, I think it would be silly to ignore the defensive general, Vasquez. He always seems to have good games against Milan and honestly, he’s the type of player the Rossoneri could use right now, at least as a deputy.

It’s been incredibly hard to predict how well Milan will do so far this season, with many ups and downs. However, my gut feeling tells me that they will be able to do a whole lot better than on Thursday, especially since the key players are back from start.

My only worry is the left-hand side of the defence, with Diawara and Estupinan set to start there. As such, I’m going to go for a narrow win, with no clean sheet either. Let us know your prediction in the comments below!
